Title: Condemnation Mute: Timing & Interaction with Banishment

Messages.Author: hardyrange
Messages.Body:
Hello out there,

what is the timing of the effect of the effect to burn 1 blood when using Condemnation: Mute at  ?

Especially:

If the referendum that passes is a Banishment, which chose the vampire with the Condemnation: Mute: Would that vampire burn one blood before she or he goes into banishment?

> Condemnation: Mute
>
> +1 stealth action. Condemnation.
> Ⓓ Lock a younger vampire.
> Requires an infernal vampire. Ⓓ Put this card on a ready vampire. The attached vampire gets -3 votes. Burn all other condemnation cards on this minion.
> As  above, and the attached vampire burns 1 blood after a referendum passes.
>
> Banishment
>
> Choose a ready younger vampire. Successful referendum means the chosen vampire is moved to the uncontrolled region (breaking any temporary control effects); any cards and counters on the chosen vampire stay with them but are out of play as long as the chosen vampire remains uncontrolled.
>
"It was a perfect plan - until it had contact with reality"

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body: IMO he does, as the referendum passes (triggering C:M) and then the results of the vote are applied.

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
Remi is correct.

Whether a referendum passes or not is determined in the "Resolve the Referendum" step of a successful political action. The effects of the referendum take place in the same step.

i.e. "after a referendum passes" is after that the effects of Banishment have been resolved.

> Rulebook:
> 3. Resolve the Referendum: If there are more votes for the referendum than against, it passes, and the effects take place. Otherwise, the referendum fails and has no effect. Tied referendums fail.
>
As the Banishment referendum passes the cards on the vampire (including Condemnation: Mute) are put out of play and thereby no effects from those cards can trigger "after a referendum passes".
